question: Summarize the page about the 2021 NBA Finals.

message.content:
The 2021 NBA Finals saw the Milwaukee Bucks defeat the Phoenix Suns in a seven-game series, winning 4-2 to claim their second NBA championship, the first since 1971. The series was played in the NBA's "bubble" at Walt Disney World in Orlando, Florida, due to the COVID-19 pandemic [4].

The Suns, who had not appeared in the Finals since 1993, made a historic run to the championship series after missing the playoffs for ten seasons and holding the worst record (.302 winning percentage) in five seasons prior to their Finals appearance [4]. The Bucks, meanwhile, were the fifth team in NBA Finals history to overcome a 2–0 deficit [4].

Giannis Antetokounmpo was the dominant force for the Bucks, leading the team in scoring, rebounding, and winning the Finals MVP award [1]. He recorded multiple 40-point games, including a 41-point, 13-rebound, 6-assist performance in Game 3, and a historic 50-point, 14-rebound, 5-block game in Game 6 to clinch the title [5]. His 35.2 points, 13.2 rebounds, and 5.0 assists per game in the series were instrumental [1].

The series began with the Suns winning Game 1 and Game 2, with Chris Paul scoring 32 points in Game 1 and Devin Booker contributing significantly [3][5]. The Bucks responded by winning Games 3 and 4, with Giannis dominating in Game 3 and Khris Middleton scoring 40 points in Game 4 [5]. The series shifted back to Phoenix for Game 5, where Jrue Holiday's steal and alley-oop pass to Giannis sealed a 123-119 victory, giving the Bucks a 3-2 series lead [5]. The decisive Game 6 was held at Milwaukee, where Antetokounmpo's 50-point performance secured the championship with a 105-98 win [5].

The 2021 Finals marked the first time since 2007 that the previous year's champions (the Los Angeles Lakers) were eliminated in the first round [4]. It was also the first time since 2007 that both Finals teams had not reached the Finals for over two decades [4].

passages.heading: 2021 NBA playoffs
passages.text:
The **2021 NBA playoffs** was the postseason tournament of the National Basketball Association's 2020–21 season. Due to COVID-19 pandemic impacting the NBA for the second consecutive year, the regular season was reduced to 72 games for each team and the start date was moved to May from its usual mid-April. It began on May 22 and concluded on July 20 with the Milwaukee Bucks defeating the Phoenix Suns in the 2021 NBA Finals. It was Milwaukee's second NBA championship, after 1971. The Bucks were also the fifth team in NBA Finals history to overcome a 2–0 deficit.

The Los Angeles Lakers were the defending champions, but lost to the Suns in the first round. With the Miami Heat losing to the Bucks in the first round, this marked the first time since 2007 that the previous year's finalists were eliminated in the first round.

passages.heading: Overview
passages.text:
- The Orlando Magic missed the playoffs for the first time in three years.
- The San Antonio Spurs returned to the postseason after missing the playoffs the previous year but were eliminated after losing to Memphis in the first stage of the Page–McIntyre system tournament.
- The Golden State Warriors returned to the postseason after missing the playoffs the previous year, being the first team to be eliminated from the Page–McIntyre system tournament with the double chance. They were the No. 8 seed, losing to the No. 7 Los Angeles Lakers in the first game of the first stage, then losing to No. 9 Memphis in the second game of the first stage.

passages.heading: Notable occurrences
passages.text:
- Deandre Ayton became the first player in NBA history to average 15 points and 10 rebounds while shooting at least 65% from the field in a single postseason.
- Jae Crowder now owns the longest active finals streak when the Phoenix Suns made the NBA Finals, having also made it last year with Miami.
- Chris Paul became the oldest player in NBA history with 40+ points in a closeout game. He is also the second oldest player to drop 40 points in any playoff game.
- With Rajon Rondo losing in the Western Conference finals to the Suns, Shaquille O'Neal's 37–year streak of having a former teammate in the NBA Finals came to an end.
- The Phoenix Suns became the first team in NBA history to move on to the NBA Finals after missing the postseason in the prior ten seasons. They also held the worst record (.302 winning pct) in five seasons prior to an appearance in the final postseason round in the history of the NBA, NFL, NHL, or MLB.
- Both NBA finalists in the 2020–2021 season have not been in the finals for over two decades (the Suns in 1993, the Bucks in 1974).
- Trae Young became the second player in NBA history to average 28+ PPG and 9+ APG in a single playoff run (minimum 15 games, LeBron James in 2018).
- Trae Young tied LeBron James and Dirk Nowitzki by scoring the 4th most points in a Conference finals game with 48 against the Milwaukee Bucks.
- Giannis Antetokounmpo became the 5th player in NBA history with 9+ 30/10 games in a single postseason since 1963.

01:31:202021 Finals Game 1: Chris Paul & Devin Booker combine for 59 in opening winChris Paul had 32 points and nine assists in an NBA Finals debut that was well worth the wait, Devin Booker scored 27 points and the Suns beat the returning Giannis Antetokounmpo and his Milwaukee Bucks 118-105 in Game 1.

01:34:182021 Finals Game 2: Booker, Bridges and Suns' depth show shooting abilityDevin Booker scored 31 points, Chris Paul had 23 and the Suns beat Milwaukee 118-108 to take a 2-0 series lead. Giannis Antetokounmpo had 42 points and 12 rebounds in his second game back after missing two games.

01:33:472021 Finals Game 3: Giannis dominates in the post to get Bucks rollingGiannis Antetokounmpo had 41 points, 13 rebounds and six assists in the NBA Finals' return to Milwaukee, and the Bucks pounded Phoenix 120-100, cutting the Suns' lead to 2-1.

01:34:022021 Finals Game 4: Bucks even the series behind Khris MiddletonKhris Middleton scored 40 points to send the Bucks past the Phoenix Suns 109-103 to tie the series 2-2. Giannis Antetokounmpo had 26 points, 14 rebounds and eight assists as his streak of 40-point games ended at two.

01:31:212021 Finals Game 5: Milwaukee steals road game as Holiday, Giannis shineJrue Holiday's steal and alley-oop pass to Giannis Antetokounmpo for a dunk sealed a wild Game 5 and gave the Bucks a 123-119 victory over the Suns. Antetokounmpo had 32 points, nine rebounds and six assists.

01:34:172021 Finals Game 6: Giannis puts on historic, 50-pt performance in close-out victoryGiannis Antetokounmpo held the Larry O'Brien Trophy in one arm and the NBA Finals MVP trophy in the other after scoring 50 points, 14 rebounds and five blocked shots as the Bucks beat the Phoenix Suns 105-98 to win the series 4-2.
